q: Under Division II of Schedule III, a liability is classified as current when, among other conditions:
o: It is due to be settled within twelve months, regardless of any deferral right
The company has no unconditional right to defer settlement for twelve months
It is expected to be settled within the normal operating cycle only
It arises from a transaction with a related party of the company
why: A liability is current if it is expected to be settled in the normal operating cycle, is held primarily for trading, is due within twelve months, or the company does not have the right at the end of the reporting period to defer settlement for at least twelve months after the reporting period. The absence of an unconditional deferral right is the decisive test.

q: A five year term loan became payable on demand due to a covenant breach before the reporting date. The lender agreed not to demand payment, but only after the reporting date. Under Division II read with Ind AS 1, the loan is:
o: Non-current, as the waiver came before the statements were approved
Current, as the right to defer did not exist at the reporting date
Non-current, as the original tenure of the loan exceeds twelve months
Split between current and non-current per the repayment schedule
why: Classification depends on the position at the end of the reporting period. Because the right to defer settlement for at least twelve months did not exist at that date, the loan is current, and the post reporting date waiver is a non-adjusting event requiring disclosure only.

q: The trade receivables ageing schedule under Division II of Schedule III uses which buckets?
o: Less than 6 months, 6 months to 1 year, 1 to 2 years, 2 to 3 years, over 3 years
Not due, less than 1 year, 1 to 2 years, 2 to 3 years, 3 to 5 years, over 5 years
Not due, under 6 months, 6 months to 1 year, 1 to 2, 2 to 3, over 3 years
Not due, less than 3 months, 3 to 6 months, 6 months to 1 year, over 1 year
why: The prescribed format shows outstanding for the following periods from the due date of payment, with columns for less than 6 months, 6 months to 1 year, 1 to 2 years, 2 to 3 years and more than 3 years, and a separate line for amounts not due. Ageing runs from the due date, not the invoice date.

q: In the trade receivables ageing schedule, the rows to be presented separately include:
o: Undisputed and disputed receivables, each split good and doubtful
Secured and unsecured receivables, each split into good and doubtful
Receivables from related parties and from other parties only
Receivables at amortised cost and those at fair value only
why: The format requires separate rows for undisputed trade receivables considered good, undisputed considered doubtful, disputed considered good and disputed considered doubtful. Related party split is a separate disclosure and not the basis of the ageing rows.

q: Under Division II of Schedule III, the ageing schedule for capital work-in-progress must be given with the buckets:
o: Less than 6 months, 6 months to 1 year, 1 to 2 years, over 2 years
Less than 1 year, 1 to 2 years, 2 to 3 years and more than 3 years
Not due, less than 1 year, 1 to 3 years, 3 to 5 years, over 5 years
Less than 1 year, 1 to 3 years, 3 to 5 years, more than 5 years
why: The CWIP ageing schedule uses amount in CWIP for a period of less than 1 year, 1 to 2 years, 2 to 3 years and more than 3 years, split between projects in progress and projects temporarily suspended. The same buckets apply to intangible assets under development.

q: For capital work-in-progress projects whose completion is overdue or which have exceeded their cost compared to the original plan, Division II of Schedule III requires:
o: A separate note giving only the reasons for the cost overrun
A project-wise completion schedule in the same four time buckets
Immediate impairment of the cost in excess of the original plan
Disclosure only where project cost exceeds ten percent of gross block
why: Where completion is overdue or cost has exceeded the original plan, a separate completion schedule is required project-wise showing the amounts expected to be spent, bucketed as less than 1 year, 1 to 2 years, 2 to 3 years and more than 3 years. There is no ten percent trigger and no automatic impairment.

q: The promoter shareholding disclosure under Division II of Schedule III requires, for each promoter:
o: Number of shares and percentage of total shares held, and nothing more
Shares held at the year end and the percentage change in the year
Shares at year end, percentage of total shares and percentage change
Shares held at the beginning of the year and any pledge created on them
why: The prescribed table for shares held by promoters at the end of the year shows promoter name, number of shares, percentage of total shares and percentage change during the year, with comparatives for the previous year. Pledge details are not part of this table.

q: Where title deeds of immovable property are not held in the name of the company, Division II of Schedule III requires disclosure of all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Description of the item of property and its gross carrying value
Name in which the title deed is held and whether that person is a promoter
The period for which the property has been held and the reason for it
The stamp duty and registration charges payable on future transfer
why: The prescribed table covers the description and gross carrying value, the name in which the title deed is held, whether that holder is a promoter, director or relative or employee of a promoter or director, the period held and the reason for not being in the company name. Prospective stamp duty is not a required disclosure.

q: Which of the following ratios is NOT among those specifically required to be disclosed under Division II of Schedule III?
o: Debt-Equity Ratio, being total debt over shareholder equity
Trade Receivables Turnover Ratio, based on credit sales
Return on Capital Employed, based on earnings before interest and tax
Price-Earnings Ratio, being market price over earnings per share
why: The prescribed list includes current ratio, debt-equity, debt service coverage, return on equity, inventory turnover, trade receivables turnover, trade payables turnover, net capital turnover, net profit ratio, return on capital employed and return on investment. Price-earnings is a market ratio and is not part of the list.

q: When disclosing the required ratios under Division II of Schedule III, the company must:
o: Disclose the ratio for the current reporting year alone
Disclose the ratio and explain changes of 25 percent or more
Disclose the ratio and explain changes of 10 percent or more year on year
Disclose the ratio and reconcile it with the industry average figure
why: The instruction requires disclosure of the numerator and denominator along with explanation of items included, and an explanation is required where there is a change of 25 percent or more as compared to the preceding year. A 10 percent threshold is not prescribed.

q: Regarding relationship with struck-off companies, Division II of Schedule III requires disclosure of:
o: Name, nature of transactions, balance outstanding and relationship
Only investments held in companies struck off under Section 248
Only balances outstanding that exceed Rs 1 lakh at the year end
Only transactions with companies struck off during the reporting year
why: The disclosure covers transactions with companies struck off under Section 248 of the Companies Act 2013 or Section 560 of the Companies Act 1956, giving the name, nature of transactions such as investments, receivables, payables or shares held, the balance outstanding and the relationship with the struck off company. There is no monetary threshold.

q: Where a company has borrowings from banks or financial institutions on the security of current assets, Division II of Schedule III requires disclosure of:
o: Whether quarterly statements agree with books, with reconciliation
Only the sanctioned limit and the amount utilised at the year end
The reconciliation only where sanctioned limits exceed Rs 5 crore
The reconciliation only where a first charge on current assets exists
why: The disclosure requires a statement of whether the quarterly returns or statements of current assets filed with banks or financial institutions are in agreement with the books, and where not, a summary reconciliation and reasons for material discrepancies. Unlike the CARO clause, the Schedule III disclosure has no Rs 5 crore trigger.

q: A company has total income of Rs 120 crore. Under Division II of Schedule III, the rounding off in the financial statements:
o: To the nearest lakhs, millions or crores, or decimals, used uniformly
Optional, and if adopted to the nearest hundreds, thousands, lakhs or millions
To the nearest crores only, decimals of crores not being permitted
Not permitted at all where total income exceeds Rs 100 crore
why: Where total income is Rs 100 crore or more, rounding off must be to the nearest lakhs, millions or crores, or decimals thereof. Where total income is less than Rs 100 crore, rounding to the nearest hundreds, thousands, lakhs or millions is allowed. Rounding must be used uniformly in the financial statements.

q: Under Division II of Schedule III, the basis for deciding the rounding off option is:
o: Turnover from operations for the reporting financial year
Total assets shown in the balance sheet at the year end
Total income of the company for the reporting financial year
Paid-up share capital plus free reserves at the year end
why: The rounding off instruction in Division II is keyed to total income, with the Rs 100 crore mark separating the two permitted sets of options. Earlier formats used turnover, which makes that the most tempting distractor.

q: Under Division II of Schedule III, security deposits given by a company are presented as:
o: Trade receivables, as they arise in the normal course of business
Loans in every case, whether recoverable in the short or long term
Other financial assets, split current or non-current on recovery
Other non-current assets in every case, whatever the recovery date
why: Security deposits are financial assets that do not meet the definition of trade receivables or loans, so they are presented under other financial assets, split into current and non-current based on when recovery is expected. Classifying them uniformly as non-current ignores the current or non-current test.

q: Under Division II of Schedule III, which of the following is presented on the face of the balance sheet rather than only in the notes?
o: Ageing of trade payables from the due date of payment
Reconciliation of shares outstanding at the start and end of the year
Names of shareholders holding more than 5 percent of the shares
Current tax liabilities (net) under current liabilities
why: Current tax liabilities (net) is a prescribed line item on the face of the balance sheet under current liabilities. Ageing schedules, the 5 percent shareholder list and the share reconciliation are all note disclosures.

q: In the statement of profit and loss under Division II of Schedule III, other comprehensive income must be presented:
o: As a single undivided total presented after profit for the reporting period
Only within the statement of changes in equity for the period
Within other income above profit before tax for the period
Split into items to be reclassified and not reclassified, with tax
why: Division II requires other comprehensive income to be split into two groups, items that will not be reclassified to profit or loss and items that will be reclassified to profit or loss, each with the related income tax effect. Presenting a single undivided total does not meet the format.

q: Under Division II of Schedule III, revenue from operations must be disclosed separately showing:
o: Only sale of products and sale of services, shown separately
Revenue split by geographical segment and by class of customer
Gross revenue with excise duty deducted therefrom, and nothing else
Sale of products, sale of services and other operating revenues
why: Revenue from operations is disclosed separately as sale of products including excise duty, sale of services and other operating revenues. Geographical segment disclosure is required by Ind AS 108 and is not part of the Schedule III face format.
